messages:
maya: FYI customers reported sudden uptick in quota hits for embeddings route after yesterday's sampling rollout. screenshots attached in ticket.
phil: saw that too. looks like router is using `est_units` which was multiplied by 1/(sample_rate) in the new emitter. if emitter sends sample_rate=0.2 we multiply -> big estimates.
raj: wait we should *divide* by sample_rate to estimate full-units when sampling (i.e. observed_units / sample_rate). are you saying we multiplied instead? that's backwards.
phil: exactly. the sampler PR (https://scm.redwood/PR/1823) introduced a `sample_rate` header but the router code path that handles sampled telemetry applied `* 1/sample_rate` incorrectly in one path and `* sample_rate` in another depending on which metric sink was used. inconsistent.
tj: ugh. that would cause both huge over-estimates and huge under-estimates depending on sink. can you paste the two code snippets?
phil: pasted logs and snippets: 
```
-- sink A (preagg)
adjusted = observed_units * sample_rate  -- WRONG
-- sink B (raw)
adjusted = observed_units / sample_rate  -- CORRECT
```
sofia: impact: tenants with sample_rate < 1 got throttled aggressively because router thought they used more units than they did. others looked like they used less and escaped throttles.
maya: ops bot flagged increased 429s at 03:12UTC and ticket #ENG-4987 started. we need a mitigation ASAP.
raj: mitigation options: (1) roll back emitter sampling header (2) change router to prefer sink B semantics (3) add quick UI annotation so customers know we had a sampling mismatch.
tj: we should avoid rollback if possible. safer to patch router to canonicalize on `sample_rate` semantics: treat header as fraction in all sinks and compute `estimate = observed / sample_rate` with safe-guards (cap to max multiplier of 10). patch + canary.
phil: agree. add cap (min 0.01, max 1.0 for sample_rate) and cap multiplier to 10 to avoid runaway. will PR today.
sofia: console UX: show an incident ribbon on affected tenant dashboards + link to explain why usage may diverge from billing. also expose telemetry_source in the usage table so SRE/account teams can triage quickly.
maya: ops wants tenant toggle to ignore sampled telemetry for quota decisions temporarily (per-tenant override). can we add a `quota_source` override in tenant settings?
raj: feasible. internal API: `PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}` body {"quota_source":"realtime|rollup|ignore_sampled"}. Implement router to consult tenant override before using the default heuristics.
tj: implement router change in two phases: (A) interpret sample_rate correctly + cap multiplier; (B) add tenant override + priority to prefer realtime counters. phase A to canary tomorrow, phase B next week.
phil: note on telemetry: we should version the header to `X-Embed-Telemetry-V` and make `X-Embed-Sample-Rate` optional. default sample_rate=1 if missing. also log when sample_rate < 1 for alerting.
sofia: console badge idea: small per-route tooltip that says "usage adjusted for sampling (rate=0.2)" and show the raw observed vs adjusted numbers with the query used. example: 
```
observed_units: 12,345
sample_rate: 0.2
adjusted_estimate = observed_units / sample_rate = 61,725
```
that helps explain the math to customers.
maya: client SDKs note: we also introduced a client-side sampling switch in the Node SDK. ops asked us to push a patch to log the sample_rate in client telemetry so we can correlate.
raj: will add a small change to the runtime ingestion: when sample_rate < 1, attach a `sampling_origin` tag (client|edge|splitter) to help track where sampling happened. strip the tag post-dedupe so storage cardinality doesn't explode.
tj: router sim plan: run 24h of production traffic through staging with the corrected math + caps. will validate throttle rates and 429s.
phil: PR opened: https://scm.redwood/PR/1845 includes fix + cap + tests. cc @tj for staging run.
sofia: I'll ship the console badge mock to design review and add the tenant toggle to the settings mock. link: https://redwood.internal/mockups/telemetry-sample-explain
maya: ops-bot: will we be able to roll forward without customer impact?
ops-bot: temporary mitigation: increased soft quota window by +20% for affected tenants (auto-flagged by rule). will revert after router patch validated.
raj: great. after patch and canary pass we'll run re-count job for the last 48h and reconcile console numbers with billing. also add an audit log entry for the sampling rollout.
maya: assigning follow-ups: phil -> patch PR, tj -> router sim, sofia -> console UX, raj -> ingestion tagging + audit, maya -> ops coordination. ticket ENG-4987 updated.
phil: deployed PR to staging, tests pass. ready for canary.
tj: starting canary run now. will post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
